senses.en: a customary way of operation or behavior

examples.text: It is standard practice in the industry to disclose potential conflicts of interest before publication.

senses.en: Actual operation or experiment, in contrast to theory.

examples.text: That may work in theory, but will it work in practice?

senses.en: systematic training by multiple repetitions

examples.text: Mastery of a difficult instrument demands years of disciplined daily practice.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prassō('행하다')에서 나온 praktikos가 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 들어왔습니다. 행하는 방식이 '관행'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A person who practices a profession or art, especially law or medicine.

examples.text: Experienced practitioners of the craft often disagree about which technique is best for beginners.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prassō('행하다')에서 나온 practician에 -er가 붙은 말입니다. 실제로 일을 행하는 사람을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: concerned with practical matters

examples.text: The senator took a pragmatic approach, accepting a modest compromise rather than risking the entire bill.

origin.ko: 그리스어 pragma('행해진 일')에서 왔습니다. 실제 일에 밝다는 뜻에서 '실용적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To speak incessantly and in an inconsequential or childish manner; to babble.

examples.text: The guests prattled on about the weather while the real issues went undiscussed.

senses.en: idle or foolish and irrelevant talk

examples.text: The candidate dismissed her opponent's speech as empty prattle devoid of any real policy.

origin.ko: prate('수다 떨다')에 반복을 나타내는 -le가 붙은 말입니다. 쉴 새 없이 재잘거리는 모습입니다.

senses.en: Alternative spelling of preempt.

examples.text: The company moved to pre-empt criticism by publishing its own audit before regulators could.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prae-('먼저')와 emere('사다')가 합쳐진 말입니다. 남보다 먼저 사서 차지한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A short preliminary statement or remark, especially an explanatory introduction to a formal document or statute.

examples.text: The preamble to the treaty states its purpose before listing any binding obligations.

senses.en: A precursor.

examples.text: High winds are often a preamble to a winter storm.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 praeambulum('앞서 걷다')에서 왔습니다. 본문 앞에 먼저 걸어가는 글이 서문입니다.

senses.en: Dangerously insecure or unstable; perilous.

examples.text: The firm's finances remained precarious after two consecutive years of falling revenue.

origin.ko: 라틴어 precārius('간청해서 얻은')에서 왔습니다. 남의 호의에 달려 불안정하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A decided case which is cited or used as an example to justify a judgment in a subsequent case.

examples.text: The court cited an earlier ruling as precedent when it rejected the company's appeal.

senses.en: an example that is used to justify similar occurrences at a later time

examples.text: Granting one exception could set a dangerous precedent for every future request.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praecēdere('앞서 가다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 앞서 있었던 사례가 곧 선례입니다.

senses.en: A rule or principle, especially one governing personal conduct.

examples.text: Precept guides, but example draws.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praecipere('미리 가르치다', prae + capere)에서 왔습니다. 앞서 쥐여 주는 가르침이 교훈입니다.

senses.en: done with very great haste and without due deliberation

examples.text: Critics warned that a precipitate withdrawal of troops would leave the region dangerously unstable.

senses.en: To make something happen suddenly and quickly.

examples.text: it precipitated their success

senses.en: To send violently into a certain state or condition.

examples.text: we were precipitated into a conflict

origin.ko: 라틴어 praeceps('머리부터 거꾸로')에서 왔습니다. 머리부터 내던지듯 서두르는 데서 '성급한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: dangerously steep

examples.text: The trail follows a precipitous ridge with a long drop on either side.

senses.en: Hasty; rash; quick; sudden

examples.text: […]humans have been responsible for a precipitous decline of elephants, from perhaps 300,000 in the early 1970s to some 10,000 today.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praeceps('머리부터 거꾸로')에서 왔습니다. 머리부터 곤두박질칠 만큼 가파르다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a sketchy summary of the main points of an argument or theory

examples.text: Each student submitted a one-page precis of the article before the seminar began.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 précis('간결한')에서 온 말입니다. 군더더기를 잘라 낸 요약문을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: The state of being precise or exact; especially, both exact and accurate.

examples.text: The surgeon worked with remarkable precision, leaving only a barely visible scar.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 precision에서 왔으며 precise('정확한')에서 나왔습니다. 군더더기를 잘라 내 정확해진다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: To remove the possibility of; to rule out; to prevent or exclude; to render impossible.

examples.text: It has been raining for days, but that doesn’t preclude the skies clearing by this afternoon!

origin.ko: 라틴어 praeclūdere('앞을 닫다')에서 왔습니다. 미리 문을 닫아 가능성을 막는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Characterized by exceptionally early development or maturity.

examples.text: The precocious child began reading the newspaper at age four.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praecox('일찍 익은')에서 왔습니다. 과일이 제철보다 먼저 익듯 일찍 성숙한 아이를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: something that precedes and indicates the approach of something or someone

examples.text: Economists treated the sharp drop in orders as a precursor of the coming recession.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praecursor('앞서 달리는 사람')에서 왔습니다. 먼저 달려와 뒤에 올 것을 알리는 선구자입니다.

senses.en: one who precedes you in time (as in holding a position or office)

examples.text: The new director reversed several policies introduced by her predecessor.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prae-('앞')와 dēcēdere('물러나다')에서 왔습니다. 먼저 물러난 자리의 사람이 전임자입니다.

senses.en: An unfortunate or trying position or condition.

examples.text: Stranded without money or a passport, the traveler found herself in a serious predicament.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 praedicāmentum('단정된 것, 범주')에서 왔습니다. '처한 상태'라는 뜻을 거쳐 '곤경'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: a strong liking

examples.text: The editor's predilection for long, ornate sentences often frustrated her younger colleagues.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 praedīlēctiō에서 왔습니다. 다른 것보다 먼저 골라 아끼는 마음을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: made susceptible

examples.text: Some people are genetically predisposed to heart disease regardless of their diet.

origin.ko: pre-('미리')에 dispose('배치하다')의 과거분사가 붙은 말입니다. 미리 어느 쪽으로 기울어 놓였다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To prevent or beat to the punch, to forestall an expected occurrence by acting first.

examples.text: By his statement, the Secretary-General had effectively preempted the usual frustrating debates over questions of fact and law.

senses.en: take the place of or have precedence over

examples.text: Breaking news coverage preempted the regular evening programming for several hours.

origin.ko: preemption에서 거꾸로 만든 말입니다. 라틴어 '먼저 사다'에서 남보다 앞서 차지한다는 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: designed or having the power to deter or prevent an anticipated situation or occurrence

examples.text: The government launched a preemptive campaign to calm investors before the announcement.

origin.ko: preempt에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 먼저 선수를 쳐서 막는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To spend time making oneself attractive and admiring one's appearance, e.g. in front of a mirror.

examples.text: The actor preened in front of the mirror before stepping onto the red carpet.

senses.en: pride or congratulate (oneself) for an achievement

examples.text: The minister preened over the modest gains as though they were a historic triumph.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 prēon('핀')에서 온 말로, 새가 부리로 깃털을 다듬는 모습과 prune의 영향을 받았습니다. 몸치장하는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: consider, ponder, or plan (an action) beforehand

examples.text: Prosecutors argued that the defendant had premeditated the crime for weeks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praemeditārī('미리 곰곰이 생각하다')에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: a statement that is assumed to be true and from which a conclusion can be drawn

examples.text: The argument collapses because its central premise rests on an unproven generalization.

senses.en: take something as preexisting and given

examples.text: The policy is premised on the belief that consumers will respond rationally to price changes.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 premissa('앞에 놓인 명제')에서 왔습니다. 결론보다 앞서 내놓은 것이 전제입니다.

senses.en: the power to foresee the future

examples.text: Her essay showed remarkable prescience about the effects of social media on public debate.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praescientia('미리 앎')에서 왔습니다. 일이 벌어지기 전에 아는 능력입니다.

senses.en: perceiving the significance of events before they occur

examples.text: The report proved prescient, warning of the housing collapse years before it happened.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praesciēns('미리 아는')에서 왔습니다. prae-('앞')와 sciō('알다')가 합쳐진 말입니다.

senses.en: a feeling of evil to come

examples.text: She had a vague presentiment that the meeting would end badly.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 pressentiment에서 왔습니다. 일이 일어나기 전에 미리 느끼는 예감입니다.

senses.en: The belief of something based upon reasonable evidence, or upon something known to be true.

examples.text: The presumption is that an event has taken place.

senses.en: audacious (even arrogant) behavior that you have no right to

examples.text: He had the presumption to correct the professor in front of the entire lecture hall.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praesūmptiō에서 왔습니다. 증거를 다 보기 전에 먼저 취해 놓는 '추정'입니다.

senses.en: Based on presumption or conjecture; inferred, likely, presumed.

examples.text: By late May, he was already considered his party’s presumptive nominee.

senses.en: affording reasonable grounds for belief or acceptance

examples.text: presumptive evidence

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 praesumptivus에서 왔습니다. 먼저 그렇다고 취해 놓은 '추정상의'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Making unwarranted presumptions or assumptions, often out of arrogance or excessive self-confidence, and thus exceeding appropriate or rightful limits.

examples.text: It would be presumptuous of me to advise someone with so much more experience.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 praesūmptuōsus에서 왔습니다. 자격도 없이 앞질러 취하려 드는 '주제넘은' 태도입니다.

senses.en: pretending with intention to deceive

examples.text: She dropped the pretense of friendliness as soon as the cameras were turned off.

senses.en: a false or unsupportable quality

examples.text: She was a plain-speaking woman without a hint of pretense.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praetendere('앞에 펼치다')에서 왔습니다. 진짜 앞에 가면을 펼쳐 놓는 것이 가식입니다.

senses.en: making claim to or creating an appearance of (often undeserved) importance or distinction

examples.text: Reviewers found the novel pretentious, its dense allusions serving to impress rather than illuminate.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 prétentieux에서 왔고 라틴어 praetendere('앞에 내세우다')와 닿습니다. 중요한 척 내세우는 모습입니다.

senses.en: surpassing the ordinary or normal

examples.text: The old sailor had a preternatural ability to sense a storm hours before it arrived.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praeter nātūram('자연을 넘어서')에서 왔습니다. 보통 자연의 범위를 넘는 이상함입니다.

senses.en: prove superior

examples.text: The champion prevailed, though it was a hard fight

senses.en: To be current, widespread, or predominant; to have currency or prevalence.

examples.text: In his day and age, such practices prevailed all over Europe.

senses.en: use persuasion successfully

examples.text: He prevailed upon her to visit his parents

origin.ko: 라틴어 praevaleō('더 힘이 세다')에서 왔습니다. 남보다 힘이 앞서 이긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: be deliberately ambiguous or unclear in order to mislead or withhold information

examples.text: Pressed about the missing funds, the treasurer prevaricated and changed the subject.

origin.ko: 라틴어 praevāricārī('비뚤게 걷다')에서 왔습니다. 다리를 벌리고 비틀거리듯 말을 얼버무리게 되었습니다.

senses.en: The state or condition of being prime or first, as in time, place, rank, preference etc.

examples.text: The report stresses the primacy of evidence over personal opinion in policy decisions.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 primatia에서 왔으며 prime에 -acy가 붙은 말입니다. 첫째 자리에 있는 상태입니다.

senses.en: First in importance, degree, or rank.

examples.text: Our prime concern here is to keep the community safe.

senses.en: the period of greatest prosperity or productivity

examples.text: The sculptor produced her finest work in the prime of her career.

senses.en: fill with priming liquid

examples.text: prime a car engine

origin.ko: 라틴어 prīmus('첫째의')에서 왔습니다. 맨 앞에 있어 가장 중요하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: strongly adhering to, or heedful of, guiding beliefs or moral rules

examples.text: The principled senator resigned rather than endorse a policy she considered unjust.

origin.ko: principle에 -ed가 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 principium('첫 시작, 근본')에서 나온 원칙을 지닌 사람입니다.

senses.en: Unspoiled; still with its original purity; uncorrupted or unsullied.
senses.ko: 원래 상태 그대로의, 때 묻지 않은

examples.text: The beach back is in pristine condition after a council-led cleanup.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prīstinus('옛날의, 원래의')에서 왔습니다. 처음 상태 그대로 때 묻지 않았다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: complete and confirmed integrity; having strong moral principles

examples.text: The judge's probity was so well known that even her critics never questioned her rulings.

origin.ko: 라틴어 probitās('올곧음')에서 왔으며 probus('훌륭한, 정직한')에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: Related to procedure.

examples.text: The judge dismissed the case on procedural grounds: it wasn't the facts or the law, but just that they hadn't filed the correct forms.

origin.ko: procedure에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 prōcēdere('앞으로 나아가다')에서 '절차'의 뜻이 나왔습니다.

senses.en: (law) the institution of a sequence of steps by which legal judgments are invoked

examples.text: The company faces criminal proceedings over its handling of customer data.

senses.en: A published collection of papers presented at an academic conference, or representing the acts of a learned society.

examples.text: Her paper appeared in the proceedings of the annual linguistics conference.

origin.ko: proceed('앞으로 나아가다')에 -ing가 붙은 말입니다. 일을 한 단계씩 진행하는 법적 절차를 가리킵니다.

senses.en: the income or profit arising from such transactions as the sale of land or other property

examples.text: All proceeds from the auction will be donated to a children's hospital.

origin.ko: proceed('앞으로 나아가다')에서 나온 말입니다. 거래에서 앞으로 나오는 것, 곧 수익금입니다.

senses.en: a natural inclination

examples.text: The young poet showed an early proclivity for melancholy themes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōclīvitās('앞으로 기울어짐')에서 왔습니다. 마음이 한쪽으로 기우는 성향입니다.

senses.en: recklessly wasteful

examples.text: The prodigal heir squandered the family fortune within a decade.

senses.en: Yielding profusely, lavish.

examples.text: How can he be so prodigal with money on such a tight budget?

senses.en: Returning or having returned, especially repentantly, after such an abandonment.

examples.text: Fans welcomed the prodigal star back to the club after three years abroad.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōdigus('낭비하는')에서 왔고, prōd-('앞으로')와 agō('몰다')가 합쳐졌습니다. 재산을 마구 몰아 내버린다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe

examples.text: The young pianist displayed a prodigious memory, performing entire concertos without a score.

senses.en: of momentous or ominous significance

examples.text: a prodigious vision

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōdigium('전조, 경이로운 일')에서 왔습니다. 불가사의할 만큼 엄청나다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: an unusually gifted or intelligent (young) person; someone whose talents excite wonder and admiration

examples.text: At nine, the chess prodigy was already defeating seasoned grandmasters in public exhibitions.

senses.en: a sign of something about to happen

examples.text: Ancient chroniclers recorded the comet as a prodigy foretelling the king's death.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōdigium('전조, 불가사의')에서 왔습니다. 놀라운 일이라는 뜻에서 놀라운 재능을 지닌 아이가 되었습니다.

senses.en: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude

examples.text: After two years abroad, she became proficient in three languages.

origin.ko: 라틴어 proficere('앞으로 나아가다')에서 왔습니다. 계속 진전해 숙달되었다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: recklessly wasteful

examples.text: Critics condemned the profligate spending that left the city deeply in debt.

senses.en: unrestrained by convention or morality

examples.text: The novel portrays a profligate aristocracy indifferent to the suffering around it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōflīgāre('때려눕히다')에서 왔습니다. 쓰러질 만큼 막 써 버리는 '방탕한'의 뜻으로 번졌습니다.

senses.en: showing intellectual penetration or emotional depth

examples.text: a profound insight

senses.en: far-reaching and thoroughgoing in effect especially on the nature of something

examples.text: The invention of printing had a profound effect on the spread of literacy across Europe.

origin.ko: 라틴어 profundus('깊은')에서 왔고, pro('앞으로')와 fundus('바닥')가 합쳐졌습니다. 바닥까지 닿는 깊이입니다.

senses.en: Deep intellect or insight.

examples.text: Unfortunately, Andrew's colossal ego means people miss his profundity.

origin.ko: 라틴어 profunditās('깊음')에서 왔습니다. 바닥까지 닿는 깊이가 지적 깊이가 되었습니다.

senses.en: abundant or generous to the point of excess; copious; volubly expressed.

examples.text: The host offered profuse apologies for the delay and a second round of drinks.

origin.ko: 라틴어 profusus('쏟아져 나온')에서 왔습니다. 앞으로 콸콸 쏟아지듯 풍부하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: the property of being extremely abundant

examples.text: Wildflowers grew in profusion along the roadside after the spring rains.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 profusio에서 왔습니다. 쏟아져 넘치는 풍부함입니다.

senses.en: An ancestral form of a species.

examples.text: The wolf is widely regarded as the progenitor of all domestic dog breeds.

senses.en: A predecessor of something, especially if also a precursor or model.

examples.text: ARPANET was the progenitor of the Internet.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōgenitor('앞서 낳은 사람')에서 왔습니다. 후손보다 앞선 조상을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: make a prediction about; tell in advance

examples.text: Few analysts were willing to prognosticate about the outcome of such an unpredictable election.

senses.en: indicate, as with a sign or an omen

examples.text: The bluebells may prognosticate an early spring this year.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prognōsis('미리 앎')에서 나온 중세 라틴어 prognosticare에서 왔습니다. 앞일을 미리 아는 것이 예측입니다.

senses.en: a statement made about the future

examples.text: The economist's gloomy prognostication proved far too pessimistic once exports began to recover.

senses.en: a sign of something about to happen

examples.text: The fever death-rate in May and June was abnormally high, a sure prognostication of the coming storm.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 prognosticatio에서 왔습니다. 그리스어 '미리 앎'에서 나온 말로, 미래에 대한 예측을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Costly to the extreme; beyond budget.

examples.text: I'd like to visit Europe someday, but the cost is prohibitive right now.

senses.en: Tending to prohibit, preclude, or disallow.

examples.text: Prohibitive regulations discouraged small firms from entering the market.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prohibēre('막다')에서 왔습니다. 가격이 너무 높아 아예 접근을 막는 정도라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: extend out or project in space

examples.text: A narrow balcony projected over the street from the second floor.

senses.en: To make plans for; to forecast.

examples.text: The CEO is projecting the completion of the acquisition by April 2007.

senses.en: To assume qualities or mindsets in others based on one's own personality.

examples.text: Anxious people often project their own fears onto those around them.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōicere('앞으로 던지다')에서 왔습니다. 앞으로 내던져 튀어나오는 모습입니다.

senses.en: a prediction made by extrapolating from past observations

examples.text: Official projections show the population doubling within the next fifty years.

senses.en: (psychiatry) a defense mechanism by which your own traits and emotions are attributed to someone else

examples.text: His constant accusations of dishonesty seemed less a judgment than a projection of his own guilt.

senses.en: any solid convex shape that juts out from something

examples.text: Climbers clung to small projections in the rock face.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōiectiō('앞으로 던짐')에서 왔습니다. 현재를 앞으로 던져 미래를 내다본 추정치입니다.

senses.en: a member of the working class (not necessarily employed)

examples.text: Marx predicted that the proletarian would eventually overthrow the capitalist order.

senses.en: belonging to or characteristic of the proletariat

examples.text: The writer cultivated a proletarian image despite his comfortable upbringing.

origin.ko: 라틴어 proletarius에서 왔고 proles('자손')와 관련됩니다. 자식 말고는 재산이 없는 가난한 시민을 가리키던 말입니다.

senses.en: To increase in number or spread rapidly; to multiply.

examples.text: The flowers proliferated rapidly all spring.

origin.ko: proliferation에서 거꾸로 만든 말로, 라틴어 proles('자손')와 ferre('낳다')에서 왔습니다. 자손이 불어나듯 급증합니다.

senses.en: intellectually productive

examples.text: a prolific writer

senses.en: bearing in abundance especially offspring

examples.text: flying foxes are extremely prolific

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōlificus에서 왔으며 prōlēs('자손')와 -ficus('만드는')가 합쳐졌습니다. 자손을 많이 낳듯 작품도 많이 냅니다.

senses.en: tediously prolonged or tending to speak or write at great length

examples.text: The judge grew impatient with the lawyer's prolix and repetitive closing argument.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōlixus('길게 뻗은')에서 왔습니다. 길게 늘어져 장황하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Long-windedness, tiresome length, an excess of words.

examples.text: The prolixity of the contract made it nearly impossible for ordinary readers to understand.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prolixitas에서 왔으며 prolix('길게 뻗은')에 -ity가 붙었습니다. 말이 쓸데없이 길다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: A speech or section used as an introduction, especially to a play or novel.

examples.text: The novel opens with a brief prologue set several centuries before the main events.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prologos('앞의 말')에서 왔습니다. 본 이야기에 앞서 하는 말입니다.

senses.en: Made without careful choice; indiscriminate.

examples.text: The senator was criticized for his promiscuous acceptance of donations from any interested party.

senses.en: Made up of various disparate elements mixed together; of disorderly composition.

examples.text: A promiscuous crowd of merchants, soldiers, and pilgrims filled the market square.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōmiscuus('뒤섞인')에서 왔습니다. 구별 없이 마구 섞인다는 뜻에서 '무분별한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: To make known or make public.

examples.text: Missionaries worked for decades to promulgate the new doctrine across the region.

senses.en: put a law into effect by formal declaration

examples.text: The ministry promulgated new safety regulations that take effect next year.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōmulgāre('공표하다')에서 왔습니다. 법령을 앞으로 내놓아 널리 알린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: strongly marked; easily noticeable

examples.text: a pronounced flavor of cinnamon

origin.ko: pronounce('선언하다')의 과거분사입니다. 분명하게 말해진 데서 '뚜렷한'이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: cause to become widely known

examples.text: Partisan websites propagate rumors faster than fact-checkers can correct them.

senses.en: multiply sexually or asexually

examples.text: Gardeners can propagate the shrub easily by taking cuttings in late summer.

senses.en: travel through the air

examples.text: sound and light propagate in this medium

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōpāgāre('번식시키다')에서 왔습니다. 식물을 가지치기로 퍼뜨리듯 널리 퍼뜨린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An inclination, disposition, tendency, preference, or attraction.

examples.text: He has a propensity for lengthy discussions of certain favorite topics.

origin.ko: 라틴어 propensus('기울어진')에서 나온 말입니다. 마음이 어느 쪽으로 기우는 성향입니다.

senses.en: An attribute or abstract quality which is characteristic of a class of objects.

examples.text: Matter can have many properties, including color, mass and density.

senses.en: something owned; any tangible or intangible possession that is owned by someone

examples.text: The law protects private property from seizure without fair compensation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 proprius('자기 고유의')에서 나온 proprietās가 어원입니다. 고유한 성질, 그리고 자기 소유라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: foretelling events as if by supernatural intervention

examples.text: Her warnings about the bank's collapse now seem almost prophetic.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prophētikos에서 왔으며 pro('앞')와 phēmi('말하다')에서 나왔습니다. 앞일을 미리 말한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To conciliate, appease, or make peace with someone, particularly a god or spirit.

examples.text: Villagers offered grain and wine to propitiate the angry river god.

origin.ko: 라틴어 propitiāre('호의를 얻다')에서 왔고 propitius('호의적인')와 이어집니다. 화난 신을 달래 호의를 얻는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: presenting favorable circumstances; likely to result in or show signs of success

examples.text: The calm weather made it a propitious moment to begin the voyage.

origin.ko: 라틴어 propitius('호의적인')에서 왔습니다. 신이 호의를 보여 형편이 유리하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea

examples.text: She was an early proponent of renewable energy long before it became fashionable.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōpōnere('앞에 내놓다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 주장을 앞에 내놓고 지지하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: correct or appropriate behavior

examples.text: The diplomat observed every rule of propriety during the formal state dinner.

origin.ko: 라틴어 proprietās('고유한 성질')에서 왔습니다. 자기 신분에 걸맞은 올바른 행동이라는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: lacking wit or imagination

examples.text: The film's prosaic dialogue failed to capture the drama of the story.

senses.en: not fanciful or imaginative

examples.text: I was simply making the prosaic point that we are running late.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prosa('산문')에서 왔고, prorsus('곧바로')는 pro-와 vertō('돌리다')에서 나왔습니다. 운율 없는 산문 같은 평범함입니다.

senses.en: To forbid or prohibit.

examples.text: The law proscribes driving a car while intoxicated.

senses.en: To banish or exclude.

examples.text: Many Roman citizens were proscribed for taking part in rebellions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōscrībere('공포하다, 추방하다')에서 왔습니다. 이름을 공개 명단에 써서 내친다는 뜻에서 '금지하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: convert to another faith or religion

examples.text: Missionaries were forbidden to proselytize among the local population.

senses.en: To advertise a non-religious belief, way of living, cause, point of view, (scientific) hypothesis, social or other position, political party, or other organization; to convince someone to join such a cause or organization or support such a position; to recruit someone.

examples.text: He has strong political views, and an annoying habit of proselytizing at parties.

origin.ko: 그리스어 prosēlytos('새로 온 사람, 개종자')에서 왔습니다. 남을 자기 종교로 끌어들이는 일입니다.

senses.en: Likely or expected to happen or become.

examples.text: Prospective students are those who have already applied to the university, but have yet to be admitted.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 prospectivus에서 왔습니다. 앞을 내다본다는 뜻에서 '장래의'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Exceedingly variable; readily assuming different shapes or forms.

examples.text: The actor's protean talent allowed him to play a villain, a saint, and a clown in one season.

origin.ko: 그리스 신화의 바다 신 프로테우스(Proteus)에서 왔습니다. 모습을 마음대로 바꿨다는 데서 '변화무쌍한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Food, especially for livestock.

examples.text: The farmers stored enough provender in the barn to feed the herd through the winter.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 provendre('지급분')에서 왔고 라틴어 praebenda('지급액')로 거슬러 갑니다. 가축에게 주는 사료입니다.

senses.en: providing carefully for the future

examples.text: A provident family, they saved a portion of every paycheck for emergencies.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvidēre('미리 보다')의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 앞일을 미리 보고 대비합니다.

senses.en: peculiarly fortunate or appropriate; as if by divine intervention

examples.text: A providential rainstorm arrived just in time to save the withering crops.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvidentia('미리 내다봄, 섭리')에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 신의 섭리처럼 운 좋게 들어맞는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Not cosmopolitan; limited in outlook; narrow; illiberal.

examples.text: Critics dismissed the mayor's views as provincial and blind to the wider world.

senses.en: of or associated with a province

examples.text: provincial government

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvincia('속주')의 형용사형 prōvinciālis에서 왔습니다. 수도에서 먼 지방 사람처럼 시야가 좁다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: under terms not final or fully worked out or agreed upon

examples.text: The provisional government promised elections once order had been restored.

origin.ko: provision에 -al이 붙은 말입니다. 라틴어 '미리 보고 마련함'에서 왔고, 임시로 마련한 것이라는 뜻으로 쓰입니다.

senses.en: serving or tending to provoke, excite, or stimulate; stimulating discussion or exciting controversy

examples.text: The professor's provocative lecture sparked a heated debate that lasted well past the hour.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvocāre('불러내다')에서 왔습니다. 상대를 앞으로 불러내 반응을 끌어내는 성질입니다.

senses.en: To cause someone to become annoyed or angry.

examples.text: Don't provoke the dog; it may try to bite you.

senses.en: call forth (emotions, feelings, and responses)

examples.text: The film's final scene provoked an unexpected burst of laughter from the audience.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prōvocāre('불러내다')에서 왔습니다. 싸우자고 앞으로 불러내는 데서 '도발하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: Skillfulness or extraordinary ability in a particular area of expertise; dexterity, mastery, or proficiency.

examples.text: The young chef's culinary prowess earned her a Michelin star within three years.

senses.en: Distinguished bravery or courage, especially in battle; heroism.

examples.text: The knight was celebrated throughout the kingdom for his prowess in battle.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 proesce('용맹, 훌륭함')에서 왔습니다. 전투에서의 용맹이 뛰어난 기량이 되었습니다.

senses.en: An agent or substitute authorized to act for another person.

examples.text: Shareholders who cannot attend the meeting may appoint a proxy to vote on their behalf.

senses.en: A measurement of one physical quantity that is used as an indicator of the value of another.

examples.text: Researchers often use tree rings as a proxy for past climate conditions.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 procuracie('대리권')의 줄임말로, 라틴어 prōcūrāre('관리하다')에서 왔습니다. 남을 대신해 돌보는 사람입니다.

senses.en: A person who is or tries to be excessively proper, especially one who is easily offended by matters of a sexual nature.
senses.ko: 점잔 빼는 사람, 지나치게 도덕적인 사람

examples.text: Her brother teased her as a prude whenever the conversation turned to romance.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 prude('훌륭한 여자')에서 왔습니다. 처신이 훌륭하다는 칭찬이 지나치게 점잔 빼는 사람이라는 뜻으로 변했습니다.

senses.en: careful and sensible; marked by sound judgment

examples.text: It is prudent to consult a physician before beginning any new exercise regimen.

senses.en: Frugal; economical; not extravagant.

examples.text: Only prudent expenditure may provide quality within a restrictive budget.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prūdēns는 prōvidēns('미리 보는')가 줄어든 말입니다. 앞일을 내다보니 신중합니다.

senses.en: characterized by lust

examples.text: The tabloid fed a prurient public appetite for details of the scandal.

senses.en: Curious, especially inappropriately so.

examples.text: Neighbors showed a prurient interest in the details of the couple's divorce.

origin.ko: 라틴어 prūriēns('가려워하는')에서 왔습니다. 근질거리는 욕망에서 '음탕한'이 되었습니다.
